pr_title: Use ForeignKey target accessors instead of splitting colspecs
pr_body:
Alembic located the target of a ForeignKey by rendering it to a dotted
string with ForeignKey._get_colspec() and splitting that string on ".".
A dot inside a schema, table or column name cannot be told apart from
the separator between those names, so a foreign key whose target name
contains a dot was mis-parsed by autogenerate rendering as well as by
batch migrations.

SQLAlchemy 2.1 tracks the target as its individual names and exposes
them as ForeignKey.target_tokens, along with ForeignKey.target_table_key
and ForeignKey.target_column.  These are wired in through three
sqla_compat helpers, _fk_target_tokens(), _fk_target_table_key() and
_fk_target_is_named(), each of which falls back to the equivalent
pre-2.1 accessor when running against SQLAlchemy 2.0.
SchemaObjects._parse_table_key() is removed, as nothing splits a table
key any longer.

Fixes #1860

Co-authored-by: Mike Bayer <mike_mp@zzzcomputing.com>
Closes: #1861
Pull-request: https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/pull/1861
Pull-request-sha: 30e3e217e404f43423c52b5ae0a66f4ed1929e94

Change-Id: I1c6a854a1df946c8023cf8c096beaaf12c0fbfbe

diff --git a/alembic/operations/batch.py b/alembic/operations/batch.py
index a32cbb36..248f2add 100644
--- a/alembic/operations/batch.py
+++ b/alembic/operations/batch.py
@@ -402,7 +402,7 @@ class ApplyBatchImpl:
     def _setup_referent(
         self, metadata: MetaData, constraint: ForeignKeyConstraint
     ) -> None:
-        referent_schema, tname, _ = _fk_target_tokens(constraint.elements[0])
+        referent_schema, tname, _ = _fk_target_tokens(constraint.elements[1])
 
         if tname != self.temp_table_name:
             key = _get_table_key(tname, referent_schema)
diff --git a/alembic/util/sqla_compat.py b/alembic/util/sqla_compat.py
index 51ea5aa6..c4f2fdd2 100644
--- a/alembic/util/sqla_compat.py
+++ b/alembic/util/sqla_compat.py
@@ -386,7 +386,7 @@ def _fk_target_is_named(fk: ForeignKey) -> bool:
     """
     fk_any: Any = fk
     if sqla_2_1:
-        return fk_any.target_column is None
+        return fk_any.target_column is not None
     else:
         return isinstance(fk_any._colspec, str)
